rules: sound may take foreground when it can tell action better than narration
dialogue may change delivery per replica without changing character voice
silence and bridge handoffs are preferred to continuous decoration
use acoustic space and sparse plausible events before decorative beds
do not compete with the real place around the listener
silence is often the correct choice
keep narration dominant and avoid subtle low-level cues that disappear in motion
reserve foreground sound for short unmistakable transitions
do not turn prose into continuous radio drama by default
use music or sound mainly for chapter openings, transitions, memories, dreams or exceptional scenes
sound must reinforce comprehension or memory rather than novelty
avoid effects during cognitively dense explanations
use short cues and silence to structure attention

universal_rules: the listener follows the story, not the engine
one primary attention owner per beat
no narration duplicates an obvious sound
every continuous layer needs a narrative reason
measured rendered speech timing is authoritative after TTS
density none is always a valid outcome
